nodes.name: NiFe LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.580 g) and Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (0.250 g) were dissolved in deionized water (40 mL) as solution A. NH4F (0.167 g) and urea (1.20 g) were dissolved in deionized water (40 mL) as solution B. A mixture of solutions A and B were added to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave (TSSA), which was heated at 160°C for 12 h. The powder was centrifuged and ultrasonicated with water and ethanol several times and then dried at 80°C.

nodes.name: NiFe LDH Electrode Preparation
nodes.procedure: A solution of water (490 μL), 5 wt% Nafion solution (15 μL), and ethanol (495 μL) was prepared. Then, NiFe LDHs (5 mg) were added to the solution to obtain a catalyst ink. The ink was placed on CP and finally the electrode was dried at 80°C overnight.

nodes.name: Li-NiFe LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Li-NiFe LDHs were prepared through a procedure similar to that for NiFe LDHs, with addition of Li2SO4 (0.012 g) to solution A: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.580 g), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (0.250 g), and Li2SO4 (0.012 g) dissolved in 40 mL DI water (solution A); NH4F (0.167 g) and urea (1.20 g) in 40 mL DI water (solution B). Mixed solutions transferred to Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave, heated at 160°C for 12 h. Product centrifuged, washed with water/ethanol, dried at 80°C.

nodes.name: Li-NiFe LDH Electrode Preparation
nodes.procedure: A solution of water (490 μL), 5 wt% Nafion solution (15 μL), and ethanol (495 μL) was prepared. Then, Li-NiFe LDHs (5 mg) were added to the solution to obtain a catalyst ink. The ink was placed on CP and finally the electrode was dried at 80°C overnight.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows typical diffraction peaks for NiFe LDHs indexed to α-phase Ni(OH)2 (JCPDS 38-0715) and β-phase Ni(OH)2 (JCPDS 14-0117); Li-NiFe LDHs peaks shift to higher angles due to lattice shrinkage from Li doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD results in Figure 2a showed the typical diffraction peaks for NiFe LDHs, which consisted of two sets of peaks... Compared with NiFe LDHs, the diffraction peaks of Li-NiFe LDHs shifted to higher values.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Li 1s peak at 56.61 eV indicating Li-OH bonds; Ni 2p peaks shift to higher binding energy (Ni2+/Ni3+ ratio changes from 6.1:3.9 to 4.4:5.6); Fe 2p shows Fe3+ peaks with high binding energy shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: First, in contrast to the initial NiFe LDHs, it can be seen that there is a characteristic peak of the lithium ion for Li-NiFe LDHs at 56.61 eV in Figure 2b... The Ni2+/Ni3+ ratio changed from 6.1:3.9 for NiFe LDHs to 4.4:5.6 for Li-NiFe LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both NiFe LDHs and Li-NiFe LDHs exhibit uniform flowerlike morphology assembled from ultrathin nanoplates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a exhibits different magnified SEM images of the NiFe LDHs. The material has a uniform flowerlike morphology... the morphology of Li-NiFe LDHs retained a nanoflower shape.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and O throughout the nanoflowers for both NiFe LDHs and Li-NiFe LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM and corresponding EDX elemental mapping (Figure 3b) results indicated that elemental nickel, iron, and oxygen were all uniformly distributed... Ni, Fe, and O were also uniformly distributed throughout the nanoflower.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDHs show (101) lattice spacing of 0.269 nm; Li-NiFe LDHs show compressed (101) spacing of 0.268 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A typical lattice spacing for the NiFe LDHs was about 0.269 nm (Figure 3c), which belonged to the (101) lattice plane... The spacing of the (101) lattice plane in Li-NiFe LDHs decreased to 0.268 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance Cdl is 2.1 mF cm^-2 for NiFe LDHs and 12.5 mF cm^-2 for Li-NiFe LDHs, indicating ~6x higher ECSA for Li-NiFe LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl of Li-NiFe LDHs was 12.5 mF cm^-2, which was almost 6 times that of NiFe LDHs (2.1 mF cm^-2).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Li-NiFe LDHs have lower charge-transfer resistance Rct than NiFe LDHs, indicating faster electron transport.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with NiFe LDHs, the Li-NiFe LDHs had a low charge-transfer resistance, which implied rapid electron transport.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS valence-band spectra show band gap of 0.85 eV for NiFe LDHs and 0.38 eV for Li-NiFe LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the XPS results of valence-band spectra have been measured (Figure S1 in the Supporting Information); the corresponding band gaps were calculated to be 0.38 and 0.85 eV for Li-NiFe LDHs and NiFe LDHs, respectively.
